newsitem.title: GREECE: RALLYING-SAINZ HANDED VICTORY, BACK IN TITLE CONTENTION.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-SAINZ HANDED VICTORY, BACK IN TITLE CONTENTION.

text.p: Carlos Sainz of Spain stormed into contention for a third world championship title on Tuesday when Juha Kankkunen pulled over to let his senior team mate win the Acropolis Rally.
Sainz crossed the line for his first victory this season, beating Kankkunen of Finland by 17 seconds.
Kankkunen led for most of the race but was ordered by Ford officials to slow down to allow Sainz the victory.

"This result proves many things and it is a wonderful day for everyone in the team," said Sainz, world champion in 1990 and 1992. "This season has been an incredible challenge and I believe this victory is just reward for everyone at Ford."
Briton Richard Burns, in a Mitsubishi, was initially given third place, but was later dropped to back to fourth behind reigning world champion Tommi Makinen after incurring two time penalties.
Sainz's victory saw him close to within 14 points of current leader Makinen in a Mitsubishi and left him four behind Briton Colin McRae after eight rounds of the championship.

"I think we are in a better position and I am back challenging for the world championship and see no reason why we cannot win any more rallies having won the toughest European event of the season," said Sainz, who had written off his title chances after the last round of the series in Argentina.
McRae's retirement on the second stage and Makinen's tyre and driveshaft problems on the second day left the way open for Ford's and Sainz's first win since Indonesia last year.
Sainz had spent much of the rally behind Kankkunen, who last won an event in 1994, after losing more than one minute on the opening day when he slid into a bank on the fourth stage.
But on the second day he set the fastest time on six of the day's seven stages to start the final leg 37 seconds behind Kankkunen.
The Spaniard reduced that gap steadily over the final day to move to within 16 seconds of the lead on the 18th stage, before Kankkunen allowed him to take the lead.
Kankkunen came home second to give Ford their first one-two since the Rally of Portugal in 1993.
